reason: Round 0 review covers all 52 items and both assigned pages. The conditional model scope is broadly sound, but several local prerequisite proofs and the fluid-symbol example need one repair pass before acceptance.

findings.reason: Step 3.1 uses completeness of H^k to pass Cauchy products to a limit, then says completeness follows from the weighted Fourier norm without proving it or declaring a supplier. The earlier lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-completeness supplies the exact result; cite it and record the dependency.

Part (d) concludes that the complete reduced dust system is symmetric hyperbolic, but this item proves only the E/B curl-block bound and its dependencies do not supply the other equation blocks. Those transport equations first appear in lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations, which itself depends on this item. Supply the full principal-block argument here without an undeclared later premise, or separate the block-symbol result from the full-system conclusion.

Fact [L5] invokes periodic-system uniqueness for H, which is defined only on an arbitrary open neighborhood U of a possibly noncompact hypersurface. The proof gives no localization or finite-speed argument transferring that periodic result to this local wave solution. Add a coordinate-cone energy proof or an explicit extension and finite-speed argument.

The supplied Gauss/Codazzi formulas concern the original metric g, while the constructed curvature slots and Ricci contractions use gamma=-g. Step 2.1 applies the supplier without stating the conversion. Explicitly carry R^gamma_{IJKL}=-R^g_{IJKL}, Ric^gamma=Ric^g, S^gamma=-S^g, and the resulting Gauss/Codazzi signs into the curvature initialization.

For signature (-+++), the stated future unit rest vector n has n-flat(n)=-1. Thus zeta=n-flat+(1/2)e1-flat evaluates to -1, not the claimed positive zeta_0=1, and its symbol is not positive. Use -n-flat+(1/2)e1-flat or recompute the symbol for the written covector.

The displayed shell sequence u_N has H^1 norm growing like 2^(5N/2); the proof establishes an unbounded C^0/H^1 ratio. Normalize the sequence or change the title, which currently claims the raw family has bounded H^1 norm.

Its sharpness remark attributes failure for every integer s-m<3/2 to the companion counterexample, which proves only the case s-m=1. Restrict the remark to that case or include the remaining integer case s-m=0.

The exclusions say vacuum boundaries are outside scope, while thm-gr-dust-local-evolution admits smooth nonnegative density and smooth zero-density regions. Distinguish excluded nonsmooth/free-boundary or junction behavior from the smooth zero sets and empty regions that the dust theorem includes.

Make the physical unit conventions explicit for the selected matter branches. In particular distinguish the normalized unit field u (g(u,u)=-1) from the SI four-velocity U (g(U,U)=-c^2), state u=U/c and the dust relation epsilon=rho_mass c^2, and specify the scalar field/potential/coupling dimensions or an explicit field-unit convention.
